source.title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS

accepted.question_text: For a general infinite-dimensional control system, does every input-to-state stability Lyapunov function given in implication form also admit an equivalent dissipative-form characterization, without imposing the restrictive extra assumptions currently needed? Equivalently, is implication-form ISS Lyapunov theory fully equivalent to dissipative-form ISS Lyapunov theory in infinite dimensions, as it is for ordinary differential equations under reasonable regularity assumptions?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.17. For infinite-dimensional systems, it is easy to see that if V is an ISS Lyapunov function in dissipative form, then it is an ISS Lyapunov function in implication form. It is, however, an open question, whether the converse implication holds unless quite restrictive requirements on Σ and Lyapunov function V are imposed, see [167, Theorem 3.4].

accepted.question_text: Can one prove local input-to-state stability by using non-coercive Lyapunov functions, and can one obtain such local results when the non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function is formulated in implication form rather than dissipative form? In other words, develop non-coercive Lyapunov criteria for LISS and for implication-form non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions in infinite-dimensional systems.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.21. Theorem 2.19, in contrast to Theorem 2.18, gives an ISS criterion only for the global ISS property, and non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions are formulated in dissipative form. Currently, there are no non-coercive Lyapunov results for the LISS property and for non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions defined in implication form.

accepted.question_text: Given an infinite-dimensional system that satisfies the local input-to-state stability estimate with comparison functions β and γ, determine or estimate the actual region in the product space of states and inputs on which that LISS estimate is valid. In particular, go beyond existence proofs and obtain usable bounds for the validity region in X × U.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.26. The proof of Theorem 2.25 is based on converse Lyapunov theorems for the 0-UAS property, see [161], and thus it does not give a precise estimate for the region in X ×U for which the LISS estimate (1.6) is valid (for given β, γ). The estimation of the region in which the LISS estimate is valid is a hard problem, which has not been touched so far for infinite-dimensional systems.

accepted.question_text: Establish converse input-to-state stability Lyapunov theorems for broad classes of infinite-dimensional systems beyond the currently covered cases, specifically for general nonlinear systems and for general linear boundary control systems. The goal is to know when ISS necessarily implies the existence of an appropriate ISS Lyapunov function in these settings.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.28. For general nonlinear systems and even for general linear boundary control systems converse ISS Lyapunov theorems are not available now and constitute an important and complex open problem.

accepted.question_text: For linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators and input space L∞(R+, U), does input-to-state stability imply integral input-to-state stability? More specifically, after knowing that iISS implies ISS in this setting, determine whether the reverse implication ISS ⇒ iISS also holds for L∞ inputs.
accepted.context_brief: ISS versus iISS for L∞ inputs

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.22. In view of Proposition 3.20 we know that for U := L∞(R+, U), integral ISS implies ISS. At the same time, the question whether ISS w.r.t. L∞(R+, U) implies iISS w.r.t. L∞(R+, U) is a challenging open problem.

accepted.question_text: Develop a satisfactory Lyapunov theory for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators. This includes deciding whether ISS always implies the existence of a coercive or non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function, whether heat equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions admit coercive ISS Lyapunov functions, whether some linear ISS systems admit only non-coercive but not coercive ISS Lyapunov functions, and whether admissibility of the input operator can be characterized in Lyapunov terms.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.31. In spite of several positive results described in this section, our present knowledge of Lyapunov methods for linear systems with unbounded operators is insufficient, and many questions are open. The very first question is whether ISS of (3.1) implies the existence of a (coercive or non-coercive) ISS Lyapunov function.

It is known that for linear hyperbolic systems of conservation laws it is possible to construct a coercive ISS Lyapunov function [216], and at the time it is unknown, whether coercive ISS Lyapunov functions exist for a heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions, or, more generally, for systems governed by analytic semigroups generated by operators with an unbounded spectrum.

Also, it is not known whether there are linear ISS control systems for which there is no coercive ISS Lyapunov function, but non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions do exist. As ISS can be characterized as the exponential stability of a semigroup combined with the admissibility of the input operator, a Lyapunov characterization of the admissibility could probably be helpful.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove full input-to-state stability, without any restriction on input magnitude, for the Burgers equation x_t = μ x_{zz} − ν x x_z on z ∈ (0,1) with boundary conditions x(t,0)=0 and x(t,1)=u(t), when the state is measured in L2(0,1) and the input belongs to a bounded piecewise-continuous input space such as P Cb(R+, R)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.12. Is it possible to prove ISS of Burgers’ equation (5.40)-(5.41) with X := L2(0, 1) and u ∈ P Cb(R+, R) (or for another input space) without restrictions on the magnitude of inputs?

accepted.question_text: For the disturbance-to-state stabilization of the considered linear hyperbolic PDE with dynamic boundary feedback, can the matrix inequality condition (5.52b) be relaxed or replaced by alternative criteria that still guarantee robustness? The broader goal is to enlarge the class of hyperbolic systems treatable by this controller-design approach.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.22. In the statement of Theorem 5.18, condition (5.52a) requires infD∈Dn+ kD(H +BK)D−1k < 1 which also appears in the more general context of nonlinear systems [43] when analyzing stability with respect to H2-norm. However, the condition (5.52b) is introduced in [215] to compensate for the lack of proportional gain in the feedback law. It definitely restricts the class of systems that can be treated with this approach and relaxing this condition or obtaining different criteria is a topic of further investigation.

accepted.question_text: Clarify the relationships between the various small-gain conditions used for infinite networks of interconnected systems, such as spectral small-gain conditions, robust strong small-gain conditions, existence of Ω-paths, and monotone invertibility of id − Γ. Use that understanding to derive input-to-state stability small-gain theorems for infinite networks with nonlinear gains.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.12. Small-gain results presented in this section use various types of the small-gain conditions: spectral small-gain condition [123], robust strong small-gain condition [53], existence of a so-called Ω-path for a gain operator Γ [53], as well as “monotone invertibility” of id −Γ [164]. The relations between these conditions are known for finite networks, but are unclear for infinite networks. Understanding of these relationships and using of this knowledge to obtain ISS small-gain theorems for infinite networks with nonlinear gains is a challenging open problem.

accepted.question_text: For time-delay systems viewed as infinite-dimensional control systems, determine whether forward completeness is equivalent to bounded reachability sets and whether the limit property LIM is equivalent to the uniform limit property ULIM. More generally, decide whether time-delay systems admit tighter ISS characterizations than those currently available from the general infinite-dimensional ISS superposition theorem.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.5. Although the ISS Superposition theorem (Theorem 2.7) is valid for time-delay systems, it is possible that for time-delay systems tighter results can be obtained.

In particular, it is not known whether forward completeness and boundedness of reachability sets are equivalent properties for time-delay systems (for the ODE case such a claim is true [143] and for general infinite-dimensional systems it is false [172]), and whether LIM and ULIM properties are equivalent notions, see [171] for more detailed discussions on this topic.

accepted.question_text: For retarded time-delay systems, is it sufficient to require a pointwise dissipation inequality of the form |x(0)| ≥ χ(‖u‖_U) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) in order to conclude ISS? Equivalently, can the stronger Lyapunov-Krasovskii hypothesis V(x) ≥ χ(|u(0)|) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) be weakened to a condition that depends only on the current state magnitude and full input norm?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.9. A question whether it is possible to weaken the requirement (7.9) further to merely
(7.10) |x(0)| ≥ χ(kukU) ⇒ V˙u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|), remains open, see [36] for some preliminary results and [35] for the positive answer of the closely related question for the iISS property.

accepted.question_text: Develop superposition theorems for integral input-to-state stability in infinite-dimensional systems that play the role for iISS that Theorem 2.7 plays for ISS. In particular, find non-Lyapunov characterizations of infinite-dimensional iISS comparable to the known finite-dimensional ODE theory.

evidence.quote: • Superposition theorems (counterparts of Theorem 2.7) are not available (for ODEs see [4, 207]).

accepted.question_text: Achieve a full understanding of the relationship between input-to-state stability and integral input-to-state stability for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators. This asks for a general structural picture, not just isolated positive or negative examples.

evidence.quote: • Full understanding of relations between ISS and integral ISS for linear systems with unbounded operators is still missing.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the existence of integral-input-to-state-stable infinite-dimensional systems that are not input-to-state stable would reveal genuine limitations of Lyapunov methods for systems with unbounded input operators, and if so, characterize how severe those limitations are. The issue is tied to the fact that ISS Lyapunov functions are automatically iISS Lyapunov functions.
accepted.context_brief: Limits of Lyapunov methods for iISS

evidence.quote: • ISS Lyapunov functions are by definition iISS Lyapunov functions. Thus the existence of iISS systems which are not ISS would suggest, that there are some limitations of the Lyapunov method at least for systems with unbounded input operators. Whether such limitations exist at all and how significant they are is a completely open question right now.

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of non-coercive integral input-to-state Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems, including their basic properties and their usefulness for proving iISS. At present this non-coercive iISS Lyapunov theory has not been investigated.

evidence.quote: • Properties of non-coercive iISS Lyapunov functions have not been investigated right now.

accepted.question_text: Substantially extend the theory of interconnections of infinite-dimensional integral-input-to-state-stable systems, whose current state is much less complete than the corresponding ISS interconnection theory. This includes sharper small-gain results and a more systematic coupling theory for iISS subsystems.

evidence.quote: • Theory of couplings of infinite-dimensional iISS systems is far less complete than in the ISS case (see [92] for a survey of such results in ODE case).

accepted.question_text: Build an integral input-to-state stability theory for bilinear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded bilinear operators. The paper identifies this part of the theory as still being in its infancy.

evidence.quote: • Integral ISS theory for bilinear systems with unbounded bilinear operators is in its infancy.

accepted.question_text: Analyze the strong iISS concept in infinite-dimensional systems, extending the finite-dimensional ODE notion and the brief discussion given in this survey. The goal is to determine its properties, scope, and role in infinite-dimensional stability theory.

evidence.quote: • Strong iISS concept, introduced in [32] for ODEs and briefly discussed in this survey (Sections 2.5, 3.6), has not been analyzed till now.

accepted.question_text: Develop an input-to-output stability theory for infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, analogous to the mature finite-dimensional IOS theory. This includes general criteria, Lyapunov tools, and structural results for systems where the quantity of interest is an output h(x,u) rather than the full state.

evidence.quote: For finite-dimensional systems the IOS theory is quite rich, see, e.g., [4, 212, 222]. There is almost no result on IOS theory in the context of infinite-dimensional systems (except for delay systems). Some exceptions include the small-gain results for IOS systems in [12, 111].

accepted.question_text: Create general ISS methods for fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional PDEs, not only for linear or semilinear equations of the form ẋ = Ax + f(x,u) with a bounded nonlinear part. In particular, extend ISS analysis to important fully nonlinear PDE classes such as porous medium and Navier–Stokes type equations, where nonlinear semigroup methods may be needed.

evidence.quote: 10.3. ISS of fully nonlinear PDEs. The absolute majority of PDE systems, which have been analyzed for robustness within the ISS framework, are either linear or belong to the class of semilinear systems, which can be written in the form (2.13).

However, many important PDEs as porous medium equation [230] and Navier-Stokes equations, do not fall into this category. This calls for looking onto a more general class of infinite-dimensional problems, which will include fully nonlinear PDEs.

For systems without inputs, the theory of nonlinear semigroups [44, 122, 159] gives a powerful method for the unified study of such equations. General methods for investigation of ISS for systems from this class are highly desirable.

accepted.question_text: Turn ISS theory into systematic robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional systems and PDEs. More concretely, develop practical ISS-based design methods for boundary or distributed robust controllers across important application areas where robust control design remains largely open.

evidence.quote: 10.4. Robust control design. As it has been already explained, the Lyapunov approach is useful for ISS analysis of PDE systems and for the design of boundary controllers ensuring an ISS property of the closed-loop system.

Many open control problems exist in the literature for robust control designs, as the drilling problem (see [193] and references therein), and the flexible structure control in aircraft (see in particular [60, 189]) to point out only a few robust control problems. Use of ISS techniques for robust control design is, to a large extent, still an open problem.
